topic: The Epic of Gilgamesh — pilot long-form documentary (40-50 min) for a new English history & mythology channel targeting US viewers
research_summary: Gilgamesh retellings are a proven but crowded format on YouTube (TED-Ed 4.4M, CrashCourse 3.1M, The Histocrat 3.6M for a 132-min video, Deep Dive History 1.28M for 111 min). Almost every existing retelling treats the text as finished. The underserved angle is that the epic is still being recovered: a looted Tablet V fragment added ~20 lines in 2014 (monkeys in the Cedar Forest, Enkidu's remorse), the looted 'Dream Tablet' was returned to Iraq in 2021, and LMU's AI 'Fragmentarium' matched 20 new Gilgamesh fragments adding detail to 100+ lines. A complete retelling that weaves in these recovered lines and the detective story of their recovery gives a differentiated, evergreen pilot with a natural hook. Conspiracy videos (US invasion to find Gilgamesh's tomb, 2.0M and 1.7M views) show demand for myth-busting that a credible channel can answer with sources.

data_points.claim: LMU's Fragmentarium identified 20 Gilgamesh fragments adding detail to over 100 lines; one tablet dates to 130 BCE, showing the poem was still copied ~2,000 years after its first known appearance
A Tablet V fragment bought by the Sulaymaniyah Museum in 2011 added ~20 new lines: a noisy Cedar Forest with monkeys, and Enkidu regretting 'we have reduced the forest [to] a wasteland'
data_points.source_name: Live Science; primary: Al-Rawi & George 2014, JCS 66:69-90

data_points.claim: The Gilgamesh Dream Tablet, looted from an Iraqi museum in 1991, was bought by Hobby Lobby for $1.67M in 2014, seized in 2019 and returned to Iraq in 2021
In November 1872 George Smith identified Tablet XI (the flood) from Ashurbanipal's library and presented it on 3 December 1872 to the Society of Biblical Archaeology, with PM Gladstone attending
Most historians think Gilgamesh was a real king of Uruk (c. 2800-2500 BC); the Sumerian King List gives him a 126-year reign; the Tummal Inscription credits him with building Uruk's walls

The earliest Gilgamesh material is a set of separate Sumerian poems (c. 2100 BC, Ur III); the oldest combined Akkadian version dates to the 18th c. BC; the 12-tablet Standard Babylonian version is credited to Sin-leqi-unninni (c. 1300-1000 BC)
The 2003 BBC headline 'Gilgamesh tomb believed found' rested on magnetometry; Fassbinder said he did not want to say definitely it was the grave, and no tomb was excavated

misconceptions.myth: It is the oldest story ever written
misconceptions.reality: It is among the oldest surviving long literary works; separate Sumerian Gilgamesh poems and other texts are older
Scholars see Mesopotamian influence, but the Tablet XI flood itself was adapted from the older Atrahasis epic; details and motives differ
Only a magnetometry anomaly was reported; nothing was excavated or verified

misconceptions.myth: The text is complete and settled

angles_discovered.name: The Oldest Epic Is Still Missing Pages
angles_discovered.hook: Humanity's oldest great epic is still unfinished - and in the last decade, looted tablets and an AI have handed us lines no one had read for 2,000 years.
angles_discovered.why_now: Tablet V lines (2014), Dream Tablet return (2021), Fragmentarium matches (2023), KASKAL 2025 report

angles_discovered.name: Gilgamesh: The Complete Epic, Rediscovered Lines Included
angles_discovered.hook: A king who was two-thirds god, a wild man made from clay, and a quest to cheat death - told in full, with the passages earlier retellings never had.
angles_discovered.why_now: Long full retellings get 1.3M-3.6M views but predate the 2014-2023 finds

angles_discovered.name: Everything You Heard About Gilgamesh Is Slightly Wrong
angles_discovered.hook: Not the oldest story, not simply copied by the Bible, and no, his tomb was not found in 2003.
angles_discovered.why_now: Conspiracy videos with 2.0M and 1.7M views; 2023 fact-check of a viral fake tomb video

angles_discovered.name: The Man Who Read the Flood
angles_discovered.hook: In 1872 a self-taught engraver read a 2,600-year-old tablet and a Prime Minister came to hear it.
angles_discovered.why_now: Evergreen discovery story; links 1872 to 2021 to AI
